## 49. Numbers roll when they change (owner request, 2026-11-24)

The owner: "make the numbers roll when they increase or decrease".

- **R1. One part does it.** `web/src/components/Roll.tsx` (styles in `web/src/styles/roll.css`) shows a number. When
  the number changes while it is on screen, each digit that changed slides to its new value like an odometer: up
  when the number grew, down when it shrank. Digits that did not change, and the other characters (".", ",", "K",
  "$"), stay still.
- **R2. Never on first load.** The first number is only shown. A roll starts only from a number that was already on
  screen, whether the new one came from live news or from a reload. A missing number ("–") never rolls.
- **R3. Timing.** One roll lasts 750 ms, slow in and slow out (`--ease-in-out`). A change in the middle of a roll
  starts a fresh roll to the newest number.
- **R4. Nothing jumps.** The number uses same-width digits and each rolling digit sits in a window one line high, so
  the tile and everything beside it keep their size. The written form is kept ("26.8K" stays "26.8K").
- **R5. Reduced motion** (the setting or the system): the number is swapped with no roll.
- **R6. Screen readers** get the final number only; the rolling digits are hidden from them. No sound plays.
- **R7. Where.** Library: the views, likes and shares totals and each post's views, likes and comments. Home: the
  views total. The Review count in the sidebar and on the tab bar. Money: every amount except the one big number
  that counts up from zero, which keeps its count-up.

## 50. Library: sort the clips (owner request, 2026-11-25)

Owner: "filter or sort the videos by something ... most relevant or most popular or from low to high in views or from
high to low ... on all, on not posted yet, and on posted ... follow the theme ... not a button ... slow in, slow out,
but the middle is fast ... phone and laptop." ADR-102.

- **S1. The sort.** A **Sort by** line at the right of the All / Not posted yet / Posted bar (its own row, at the left,
  on a phone). Four choices: **Most relevant** (the list as it came, newest first: the default), **Most popular**
  (likes, comments and shares, views break ties), **Views: high to low**, **Views: low to high**. It sorts inside the
  filter. It lives in the address (`?sort=popular|most|least`, next to `?show=`), so Back and a reload keep it.
- **S2. Not a button.** A caption, the pick and a chevron, no fill; a hairline grows under the pick on hover and
  while open. The list is the app's own (`components/Dropdown.tsx`, `variant="sort"`), glass like every menu, with a
  tick on the pick, opens below (above where there is no room) and is all in sight above the tab bar.
- **S3. Motion.** One curve opens and closes it, `--ease-unfold` (slow in, fast in the middle, slow out): it unfolds
  from its top edge in 420 ms and folds away in 340 ms, the choices follow one after another. Calm motion: no travel.

## 51. What a job's AI cost (owner request, 2026-11-25)

The owner: "when a job is finished, I want to know the exact amount that Fable cost me, and the entire process in terms
of AI usage, so tokens spent. The cost of the tokens is what I want to know at the end of a job."

- **A1. Real usage, no extra calls.** Every model answer a job gets is counted from the answer itself: Bedrock
  Converse `usage` (input, output, cache read, cache write tokens) in `agent/.../bedrock.py` (so the moment fallback,
  the second look, the checklist, captions, the picture watching by Fable and Nova 2 Lite and the layout look all
  count), the Agent SDK result's usage for picking moments, Titan's input token count, and Transcribe's audio
  seconds. A copy of a clip ("Make a copy") is a job and counts the same way. Recording is bookkeeping only.
- **A2. One price list.** `pricing` in `config/models.json`, the only place prices live: US dollars per million input,
  output, cache read and cache write tokens per model, Titan, and Transcribe per minute, each with its source, plus
  `checkedOn`. Prices come from AWS's published price lists for eu-north-1 (Anthropic's page agrees for Claude). A
  line that cannot be confirmed has `confirmed: false`: the job shows its tokens, "price not known", and the total as
  "about". `approximate: true` (Haiku 5.5 costs more above 100,000 prompt tokens) also shows "about".
- **A3. Stored on the job, additive.** `Job.aiCost` `{v, models: [{key, label, calls, inputTokens, outputTokens,
  cacheReadTokens, cacheWriteTokens, tokens, dollars?, estimated}], transcribe?: {seconds, minutes, dollars?,
  estimated}, totalTokens, totalCalls, totalDollars, estimated, pricesChecked}`. It is written with the job's own
  writes (heartbeat, ready, failed, canceled), so a failed or stopped job shows what it spent so far. A retry or
  resume adds to what the earlier runs wrote. Old jobs and jobs that never called a model have no `aiCost`: nothing
  is shown, never zeros. The API passes it through as it is.
- **A4. Not counted.** Ask, the weekly learning, lessons, campaign rules and the post-publish distil run in the API
  Lambdas, not inside a job, so they are not in a job's cost.
- **A5. The app.** The job page has one glass block, **What this cost**: the total in dollars (to the cent) large, the
  exact tokens under it, and a fold **See the details** with a row per model (calls, tokens in and out, dollars) and
  Transcribe's minutes. The numbers roll (§49). A failed or canceled job says "so far"; an estimate says "about" and
  the prices' date. The Jobs list shows the total next to the clip count of a finished job. No sparkle icon.
- **A6. Where there is no total.** Money and Home have no natural place for "AI cost this month" (they show
  earnings), so there is none.

Tests: `agent/tests/test_usage.py`, `web/test/aiCost.test.tsx`.

## 52. Attach files and images to a job's notes (owner request, 2026-11-26)

The owner: "i should be able to attach and paste images or files in general and if i want to drag and drop it will
highlight it a bit more when I hold the file and hover over the dropbox, also i should be able to delete it." Place:
the notes box on Home. BR-33, ADR-104.

- **F1. Limits.** Up to 6 files per job, 20 MB each. Allowed: images (png, jpeg, webp, gif), PDF, plain text, Markdown,
  CSV, JSON, and Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF and OpenDocument text files. Not allowed: videos (they go in "Pick a
  video") and anything else, each refused with one short sentence.
- **F2. Upload.** `POST /v1/uploads` takes an optional `purpose: "attachment"`. With it the type must be allowed (else
  400 "That kind of file can't be added.") and the size at most 20 MB (else 413 `too_large` "That file is bigger than 20
  MB."). The key is still `uploads/{userId}/{uploadId}/{filename}`, so the 14-day `uploads/` lifecycle cleans it up. No
  `purpose`: exactly as before (video only). The browser sends the file straight to S3 with the presigned PUT.
- **F3. Job create.** `POST /v1/jobs` takes optional `attachments` (at most 6) of `{key, name, type, size}`, nothing
  more per item. Each key must sit under the user's `uploads/` prefix and be safe, the object must exist and be at most
  20 MB, the type allowed, the name at most 255 characters, no key twice. Stored as `Job.attachments` only when not
  empty; old jobs have none; the API returns it as is. Retry, rerun and copies keep it. Deleting a job deletes no
  attachment (the lifecycle does).
- **F4. The agent reads them, no new model calls.** Readable: png, jpeg, webp, gif, PDF, plain text, Markdown, CSV,
  JSON. They ride in the existing prompts that already carry the owner's notes, as data that never changes the task.
  Cost bounds, named constants: text 20,000 characters per file and 60,000 across files in each prompt with the notes;
  images at most 3.75 MB and PDFs 4.5 MB and 20 pages each (unknown page count: skipped), at most 4 such blocks, sent
  only on the first Converse moment window and the captions call. A missing, expired, oversized or unreadable file is
  logged and skipped; the job never fails for it. Other allowed documents are saved only.
- **F5. The notes box.** Under the text: **Add files or images**, the hint "Logo, rules, screenshots. Up to 6 files, 20
  MB each.", then chips. Paste (Cmd or Ctrl+V) of a file or image anywhere in the Home form attaches it; a plain text
  paste still types. Drop on the notes box, or anywhere on the form for non-video files, attaches. A file held over the
  notes box lights it up with a stronger glass glow and "Drop to add", eased in and out (reduced motion: a plain fade).
  Links, Pick a video, video drops, How many clips, auto-posting and the draft work as before (a held video or a
  thumbnail with its link keeps the card's own highlight). Files can be added while the video uploads.
- **F6. A chip** shows a thumbnail or file icon, the name, the size, an eased progress bar while it uploads, and a
  remove button (44 by 44 px target, label "Remove {name}"). Remove acts at once and shows **Undo** for about 6 seconds.
  A failed file shows a short error and **Try again**; the other chips and the notes stay. A kind the agent can't read
  says "Saved, but Clip Factory can't read this kind of file." after its size.
- **F7. Make clips** waits for uploads in flight and sends only the finished ones. If a chip failed it says so in one
  line; pressing Make clips again goes on without it. Finished chips are kept in the draft as `{key, name, type, size}`.

Tests: `api/tests/test_attachments.py`, `agent/tests/test_attachments.py`, `web/test/attachments.test.tsx`.

## 53. CR active: logo and text on a clip (owner request, 2026-11-26)

The owner wants a logo and text on a clip, made after it exists, in Review. BR-34, ADR-105.

- **C1. The switch.** Each Review card has a two-state switch, **CR inactive** (the default) and **CR active**, a
  `<Glide>` bar like the other pick-one bars. Inactive: the card, Upload and posting are exactly as before. Active:
  **Edit for campaign** appears. The switch itself changes nothing a platform sees. Clip field `cr`
  `{active: boolean, campaignId?: string}`, absent on old clips (= inactive). Switching to inactive on an edited clip
  puts the original back (C5) and says "Edit removed" in a toast.
- **C2. The editor.** Only a logo and text, nothing else. A glass sheet with the clip's cover as a 9:16 preview.
  **Logo**: pick from the logo library or add one; four corner presets plus drag; a size slider (8% to 50% of the width,
  default 22%). **Text**: one short line (80 characters at most; hashtags allowed), the same presets and drag, size
  Small, Medium or Large, white with a dark edge. **When**: **Whole clip** is the default; a fold **Only part of the
  clip** takes From and To in seconds. One **Make it** button. Placement is stored as fractions (`x`, `y` = the
  element's centre, 0 to 1 of the width and height), so it holds for any size.
- **C3. One warning line.** When the logo or text box overlaps the caption band or, on a `facecam_top` clip, the
  facecam, the editor says "Under the captions" or "On the facecam" (one short line, the box turns vermilion). The areas
  are the ones the renderer draws (`agent/.../render.py`; the web copy sits in `web/src/lib/overlayAreas.ts` and a test
  pins both). HUD areas are not known, so there is no warning for them.
- **C4. The logo library.** Logos are the owner's, kept in the media bucket at `logos/{userId}/{logoId}.{png|jpg|webp}`
  (PNG, JPEG, WebP by their first bytes, at most 10 MB, at most 60 logos). Add by drag and drop, paste, or the file
  picker; each can be deleted (Undo toast); deleting a logo never changes an already edited clip (the render copied
  it). A campaign's own logo (§38) is offered too: picking a campaign (C6) copies its logo into the library once.
  - `GET /v1/logos` → `{logos: [{logoId, name, url, width, height, campaignId?, createdAt}]}` (`url` presigned, 1 h).
  - `POST /v1/logos` `{filename, contentType, size}` → 201 `{logoId, uploadUrl}`: a presigned PUT; the item is
    `LOGO#{logoId}` `{status: "uploading"}`. Also `headers` (the `Content-Type` the PUT must send). 400 on a type other than
    png, jpeg, webp or a size over 10 MB; 409 at 60 logos.
  - `POST /v1/logos/{logoId}/complete` → `{logo}`: reads the object's first bytes and size, reads width and height,
    sets `status: "ready"`; else deletes it, 400 with one sentence ("Use a PNG, JPG or WebP picture under 10 MB.").
  - `POST /v1/logos/from-campaign` `{campaignId}` → `{logo}`: copies that campaign's ready logo (once; asked again it
    returns the same logo). 404 when it has none.
  - `DELETE /v1/logos/{logoId}` → 204 (item and file).
- **C5. The edit (additive clip fields).** `overlay` `{rev, status: "working"|"ready"|"failed", error?, logo?, text?,
  timing?}` with `logo` `{logoId, x, y, size}`, `text` `{text, x, y, size: "s"|"m"|"l"}` and `timing`
  `{startSec, endSec}` (absent = the whole clip). Internal: `origVideoKey` (the untouched file), `editKey`, `overlay.startedAt`, `overlay.logo.key`.
  - `PUT /v1/clips/{clipId}/cr` `{active, campaignId?}` → `{clip}`. Only while `status == "review"` (else 409 as
    Confirm). `active: false` also does C5's reset. `campaignId` must be one of the owner's campaigns (404 otherwise).
  - `PUT /v1/clips/{clipId}/overlay` `{logo?, text?, timing?}` (at least one of logo and text; `cr.active` required,
    else 409) → `{clip}` with `overlay.status: "working"`, then asks the Clip Factory agent runtime for
    `{"action": "overlay", "userId", "clipId", "jobId", "rev"}` (no job flow, no new Lambda: the agent already has
    ffmpeg). The agent cuts nothing: it draws the logo and text on the **original** file with ffmpeg, same size, same
    audio untouched, writes `jobs/{jobId}/clips/{clipId}/edit-{rev}.mp4`, and in one conditional write (clip still in
    review, `overlay.rev` still equal) sets `origVideoKey` (when unset), `editKey`, **`videoKey` = the edited file**,
    `overlay.status: "ready"`. Every platform, the Mac helper and the download read `videoKey`, so **posting is
    unchanged**. A stale or failed render deletes its output and sets `failed` with one sentence. A render that has
    not answered after 5 minutes counts as failed (`GET` reports it).
  - `DELETE /v1/clips/{clipId}/overlay` → `{clip}`: `videoKey` back to `origVideoKey`, the edited file deleted, `overlay`,
    `editKey` and `origVideoKey` removed. The Reset button. Idempotent.
  - Confirm, Upload and auto-posting refuse or skip a clip whose `overlay.status` is `working` ("The edit is still
    being made."); nothing else about them changes (the run's schedule, count and order are untouched). Throwing a
    clip away or deleting its job removes its edited file with it.
  - The public Clip carries `cr` and `overlay` (never the keys); the `videoUrl` is the edited file once ready.
- **C6. A campaign pre-picks.** In the editor, **For campaign** lists the owner's campaigns (§38). Picking one stores
  `cr.campaignId`, selects its logo (C4 from-campaign) and puts its required hashtags (§38 rules) in the text line,
  both editable. It changes no campaign-clip rule, fit check or Confirm check (§38.8, §39); a clip that is already a
  campaign copy keeps them.

## 54. CR active: several pictures, a sheet that fits (owner request, 2026-11-26)

The owner: more than one image on a CR clip. BR-35, ADR-107.

- **L1. Layers.** A CR-active clip carries up to **4 pictures** at once (the soft cap). Tapping a library logo **adds it
  as another layer**; tapping the same logo again adds another copy. Each layer has its own place, size and time. Text
  stays one line, as in §53 C2.
- **L2. The layer list.** A small row of chips under the preview, one per picture (its thumbnail) plus the Text chip.
  The chosen chip is the one the presets, Size, drag and When change; a small **x** on it removes it. At 4: one line,
  "That's 4 pictures. Remove one to add another." and the library logos stop adding. Each picture's warning line
  (§53 C3, captions or facecam) shows for the chosen one, and a chip whose picture is covered shows a small vermilion dot.
- **L3. Stored, additive.** `overlay.logos` `[{layerId, logoId, x, y, size, timing?}]` (at most 4; `layerId` a short
  id the web makes, unique in the list; `timing` `{startSec, endSec}`, absent = the whole clip). The internal bucket
  `key` is added per layer like §53's `logo.key` and never shown. **`overlay.logo` (one picture) stays readable:** a
  clip edited under §53 has no `logos`, and everything reads its `logo` as a one-layer list; the web shows it as one
  layer and any new Make it writes `logos` and no `logo`. `overlay.timing` keeps meaning the text's time (and the
  one picture's time of a §53 edit that has no layer timing).
- **L4. API.** `PUT /v1/clips/{id}/overlay` also takes `logos` (the layers). Each `logoId` must be one of the owner's
  ready logos, `size` 0.08 to 0.5, place inside the picture, `timing` as §53; more than 4 layers is 400 "Up to 4
  pictures." `logo` is still accepted (one layer). At least one picture or the text is needed. Nothing else about
  §53 C5 changes (the original is kept, Reset, Confirm waits, auto-posting only skips a clip still being made).
- **L5. The agent.** One ffmpeg run draws every layer over the original in list order (later on top), each between its
  own start and end (whole clip by default), then the text on top. Same audio, size and encoder as §53.
- **L6. The sheet fits every screen (owner, 2026-11-27).** It never grows past the screen: head and Make it bar stay, the middle scrolls inside it. Nothing sits over anything else; text wraps inside its box. Checked at 375 to 1920 px in `web/e2e/cr-overlay.spec.ts`.
